dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:7401.text: To deliberate on an offense. Formed from 水 and 獻, with the same conception as 法.

shuowen:7402.text: To change and become soiled. Formed from 水, with 俞 indicating the sound. Alternatively, the 渝 river is at 臨俞 in 遼西 and flows east beyond the frontier.

shuowen:7403.text: To diminish. Formed from 水, with 咸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7404.text: To be exhausted or extinguished. Formed from 水, with 𤇳 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7405.text: To transport by water, as by turning a cart's hub. Alternatively, what people ride, including boats. Formed from 水, with 曹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7406.text: The palace where feudal lords hold the district archery ceremony: water lies to the southwest and walls to the northeast. Formed from 水 and 半; 半 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:7407.text: A bronze vessel receives water, with divisions marked: day and night comprise one hundred divisions. Formed from 水, with 屚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7408.text: What cinnabar transforms into: mercury. Formed from 水, with 項 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7409.text: 苹, an aquatic plant. Formed from 水 and 苹; 苹 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:7410.text: The appearance of abundant water. Formed from 水, with 歲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7411.text: To regulate water. Formed from 水, with 曰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7412.text: The appearance of thick dew. Formed from 水, with 襄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7413.text: The appearance of dew. Formed from 水, with 專 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7414.text: The appearance of weeping tears. Formed from 水, with 丸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7415.text: To disappear or be extinguished. Formed from 水, with 民 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7416.text: 沆韰 is vapor. Formed from 水, with abbreviated 䪥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7417.text: A river's name. Formed from 水, with 盧 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7418.text: A river's name. Formed from 水, with 蕭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7419.text: A river's name. Formed from 水, with 嬴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7420.text: A river's name. Formed from 水, with 除 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7421.text: A river's name. Formed from 水, with 名 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7422.text: The sound of water. Formed from 水, with 孱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7423.text: 潺湲 is the sound of water. Formed from 水, with 爰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7424.text: A great wave. Formed from 水, with 壽 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7425.text: A waterside. Formed from 水, with 敘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7426.text: A branch of water. Formed from 水, with 䢽 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7427.text: Where water stays or gathers. Formed from 水, with 豬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7428.text: Vast waters. Formed from 水, with 镾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7429.text: Vast waters. Formed from three 水. Also written 渺.

shuowen:7430.text: Clean. Formed from 水, with 絜 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7431.text: To moisten thoroughly. The source adds the incomplete phrase 'formed from.' Formed from 水, with 夾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7432.text: Sudden or abrupt. Formed from 水, with 盍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7433.text: To hold water in the mouth and spray it. Formed from 水, with 巽 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7434.text: The edge of water. Formed from 水 and 厓; 厓 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:7435.text: Two waters. The explanation is lacking. All characters in the 沝 group are formed from 沝.

shuowen:7436.text: Water moving. Formed from 沝 and 㐬. 㐬 means sudden or abrupt.

shuowen:7437.text: To wade through water on foot. Formed from 沝 and 步.

shuowen:7438.text: A riverbank, where people draw close, frowning and shrinking back, stopping without advancing. Formed from 頁 and 涉. All characters in the 頻 group are formed from 頻.

shuowen:7439.text: To frown and shrink back while crossing water. Formed from 頻, with 卑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7440.text: A small stream. The Rites of Zhou says: 'The craftsman makes ditches and channels. A plow blade is five cun wide; two blades form a pair. A furrow cut by one pair, one chi wide and one chi deep, is called 𡿨.' Twice a 𡿨 is a 遂; twice a 遂 is a 溝; twice a 溝 is a 洫; twice a 洫 is a 巜. All characters in this group are formed from 𡿨.

shuowen:7441.text: Water flowing copiously. A square hundred li constitutes a 巜 district, with a channel two xun wide and two ren deep. All characters in this group are formed from 巜.

shuowen:7442.text: Water emerging and glistening between rocks along a bank. Formed from 巜, with 粦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7443.text: Water flowing through a continuous channel. The Book of Yu says: 'Deepen the く and 巜, leading them to the rivers.' This means deepening these waters so that they join to form rivers. All characters in this group are formed from 川.

shuowen:7444.text: An underground water vein. Formed from 川 beneath 一. 一 is the earth. Abbreviated 壬 indicates the sound. Alternatively, water moving unseen along its courses.

shuowen:7445.text: Broad waters. Formed from 川, with 亡 indicating the sound. The Changes says: 'Embrace the waste and use crossing the river on foot.'

shuowen:7446.text: Flowing water. Formed from 川, with 或 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7447.text: Flowing water. Formed from 川, with 曰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7448.text: Water flowing in streams. Formed from 川, with abbreviated 列 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7449.text: Having water on all four sides, itself forming a city's moat. Formed from 川 and 邑.

shuowen:7450.text: Harm. Formed from 一 blocking 川. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: 'When a river is blocked and becomes a marsh, it is ominous.'

shuowen:7451.text: Firm and upright. Formed from 㐰, ancient-script 信, and 川, taking its unceasing flow by day and night. The Analects says: 'Zilu was firm and forthright.'

shuowen:7452.text: Habitable ground amid water is called 州; water surrounds its sides, hence repeated 川. In ancient times Yao encountered a flood and people lived on high ground amid water; some call these the Nine Provinces. The Odes says: 'On an islet in the 河.' Alternatively, 州 means a division: people divide their land and live from it.

shuowen:7453.text: A water source. It depicts water flowing out and forming a stream. All characters in this group are formed from 泉.

shuowen:7454.text: Spring water. Formed from 泉, with 緐 indicating the sound. Read like 飯.

shuowen:7455.text: Three springs. The explanation is lacking. All characters in this group are formed from 灥.

shuowen:7456.text: The source of a spring. Formed from 灥 emerging beneath 厂.

shuowen:7457.text: Long. It depicts the length of water's coursing channels. The Odes says: 'How long is the 江!' All characters in this group are formed from 永.

shuowen:7458.text: A long stretch of water. Formed from 永, with 羊 indicating the sound. The Odes says: 'How long is the 江!'

shuowen:7459.text: An oblique watercourse branching off. Formed from reversed 永. All characters in this group are formed from 𠂢. Read like the name 稗 county.

shuowen:7460.text: Blood vessels branching and coursing obliquely through the body. Formed from 𠂢 and 血.

shuowen:7461.text: To look sideways. Formed from 𠂢 and 見.

shuowen:7462.text: Where a spring emerges and connects with a river is a 谷. Formed from 水, water half visible, emerging through 口. All characters in this group are formed from 谷.

shuowen:7463.text: A mountain channel with no outlet. Formed from 谷, with 奚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7464.text: An open valley giving passage. Formed from 谷, with 害 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7465.text: An empty valley. Formed from 谷, with 翏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7466.text: A large, long valley. Formed from 谷, with 龍 indicating the sound. Read like 聾.

shuowen:7467.text: An echo in a valley. Formed from 谷, with 厷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7468.text: To deepen a channel and connect it with a river. Formed from 谷 and 𣦵. 𣦵 is damaged earth, conveying pits and hollows. The Book of Yu says: 'Deepen the furrows and channels, leading them to rivers.'

shuowen:7469.text: The green appearance of mountains and valleys seen from afar. Formed from 谷, with 千 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7470.text: Frozen. It depicts water congealing. All characters in this group are formed from 仌.

shuowen:7471.text: Water hardened. Formed from 仌 and 水.

shuowen:7472.text: Cold. Formed from 仌, with 廩 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7473.text: Cold. Formed from 仌, with 青 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7474.text: Ice. Formed from 仌, with 東 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7475.text: Ice brought out. Formed from 仌, with 朕 indicating the sound. The Odes says: 'Put it into the icehouse.'

shuowen:7476.text: Floating ice. Formed from 仌, with 斯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7477.text: Partly damaged or withered. Formed from 仌, with 周 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7478.text: The end of the four seasons. Formed from 仌 and 夂. 夂 is the ancient-script character 終.

shuowen:7479.text: To melt. Formed from 仌, with 台 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7480.text: Cold. Formed from 仌, with 倉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7481.text: Cold. Formed from 仌, with 令 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7482.text: Cold. Formed from 仌, with 圅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7483.text: Cold wind. Formed from 仌, with 畢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7484.text: 'In the first month, the wind is cold,' expressed by 㓖冹. Formed from 仌, with 犮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7485.text: Cold. Formed from 仌, with 栗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7486.text: Cold. Formed from 仌, with 賴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7487.text: Water falling from clouds. 一 depicts heaven, 冂 depicts clouds, and water falls between them. All characters in this group are formed from 雨.

shuowen:7488.text: Yin and yang press against one another and stir, producing thunder and rain that bring things to life. Formed from 雨; 畾 depicts a revolving shape.

shuowen:7489.text: Rain. People of Qi call thunder 霣. Formed from 雨, with 員 indicating the sound. Alternatively, clouds turning and rising.

shuowen:7490.text: The lingering ringing sound of thunder, which thrusts all things forth. Formed from 雨, with 廷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7491.text: 霅霅 is the appearance of thunder and lightning. Alternatively, many voices. Formed from 雨, with abbreviated 譶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7492.text: The flashing brilliance caused by yin and yang striking together. Formed from 雨 and 申.

shuowen:7493.text: A thunderclap that shakes things. Formed from 雨, with 辰 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: 'Lightning struck Yibo's temple.'

shuowen:7494.text: Congealed rain that delights things. Formed from 雨, with 彗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7495.text: Falling sleet is called 霄. Formed from 雨, with 肖 indicating the sound. This is Qi speech.

shuowen:7496.text: Millet-like snow. Formed from 雨, with 𢿱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7497.text: Rain of ice. Formed from 雨, with 包 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7498.text: Rain falling. Formed from 雨; 𠱠 depicts 𩂣, falling rain. The Odes says: 'The falling rain is fine and misty.'

shuowen:7499.text: Rain falling. Formed from 雨, with 各 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7500.text: Remaining rain. Formed from 雨, with 令 indicating the sound.
